notes: FROZEN -- agent_supports=yes, daemon_capability=incapable, no phases. muse 1.2.1-R2847.1's provider connector genuinely decodes a subscription usage window (SubscriptionUsageSnapshot{window:{used_percent,window_duration_mins,resets_at},weekly:{used_percent,resets_at},tier}, confirmed via a raw-byte scan of the real binary: 7-8 literal hits per field/type name) that maps almost field-for-field onto RateLimitSnapshot.Windows[].UsedPercent/WindowMinutes/ResetsAt (core/domain/session/rate_limit.go). But it is architecturally absent from BOTH of muse's own durable dispatch tables -- the top-level payload_type table and the nested runtime.session RunEvent event.kind table, both exhaustively extracted from the same binary -- and absent from the 212-def MSP wire schema. An exhaustive scan of all 234 on-disk session.jsonl files (including one that hit real 429 rate-limiting 22 times) found zero occurrences of any SubscriptionUsage-shaped field; the only durable rate-limit-adjacent record is a connector retry_scheduled/rate_limited status event with no used_percent/window data (relevant to the sibling 2.9 token-quota-exhausted cell, not this one). /usage (live-verified aliases /cost, /context) and /status show only token counts and context pressure -- no quota/window/reset figure anywhere, confirming there is no alternate durable or TUI-observable path either. Re-assess only if a future muse release adds a payload_type for subscription usage; a subscribed test account alone would not be sufficient since the dispatch-table absence is version-pinned, not account-state-pinned.
